purpose: Computer-context marketing concepts pending review; not uploaded.
prompts:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Create a finished premium marketing image for Pluck, a small Mac utility that lets the user select a rectangular area of the computer screen and copy recognized text. This is a generated marketing concept with fictional example content. Landscape 16:10, ideally 2560×1600.

USER DIRECTION: This must unmistakably show words ON A COMPUTER SCREEN in a useful real workflow where ordinary copying is awkward or unavailable. No outdoor physical signage, no tabletop recipe or physical note output. The visible source app/website is essential context. Pluck's own app window is not the subject and must not appear.

Visual design: warm ivory #f7f6f2 backdrop, deep forest #253b30 headline, restrained cobalt #335be5 selection and connector arrow. Modern editorial sans serif typography, generous spacing, tasteful subtle window shadow, clean front-facing desktop software screen. No photographic laptop/monitor mockups. The main application window is LARGE, taking 70–75% of the composition width and most of the bottom 70% of the image. Browser or app title bar and enough surrounding content make the computer context obvious. Window contents must be crisp and credible, not a random collection of UI pieces. Background interface text may be subdued; the source phrase must be large enough to read easily.

Top quarter: small "Pluck" wordmark top left, one large direct headline and one short supporting line. Lower area: substantial source app window, with a simple bright cobalt rectangular screen selection exactly around the example phrase, all edges horizontal/vertical, small crosshair at lower-right, no resize handles, no perspective warp. The selected words are pixels inside an image or other non-selectable source as specified, NOT ordinary chat-message or HTML body text.

A modest front-facing white digital text snippet overlaps the application's right edge, without obscuring the source phrase. Label "Copied text", black editable text matching ONLY the selected phrase exactly, plus a blue insertion caret. A single clear arrow connects selection to snippet. Snippet is plain digital surface, not physical paper or branded Pluck UI. Do not dominate the graphic with the result card. Show the source and its context clearly.

No wall of feature copy, stock illustration, invented awards, unnecessary menus, 3D objects, gradients, irrelevant decoration or tiny unreadable instructions. Correct spelling throughout. Output the complete finished image only.
Example 1: image embedded in a website.
Exact headline: "Copy words inside any image."
Exact supporting line: "Even when the website can't select them."
The source is a large believable Safari-like desktop browser window with a toolbar, address "northstar.example/events", back button and one tab. Website "Northstar" has simple nav "Events  About". Its page has a large clearly embedded PNG event poster under the visible filename label "design-night.png". Poster is colorful graphic design in blue, peach and cream, combining abstract geometric shapes and a small photograph of an auditorium, obviously one flattened promotional image, not a web text article. Poster exact prominent words: "DESIGN NIGHT", "THURSDAY, OCTOBER 22", "6:30 PM". The selection encloses only "THURSDAY, OCTOBER 22" and "6:30 PM". The result snippet contains exactly these two lines. The poster must be visibly INSIDE the website with surrounding browser UI, margins and a little page context.

Example 2: screenshot attached in Slack.
Exact headline: "Someone sent a screenshot?"
Exact supporting line: "Copy the text inside it."
Source is a large credible Slack desktop app window: muted aubergine workspace/sidebar, channel list with "# team-chat" selected, white conversation pane, ordinary message composer at the bottom. Fictional workspace "Northstar", fictional teammate "Alex". One readable message says "Here's the order confirmation." Under this message, a clearly attached raster image labeled "order-confirmation.png" contains a cropped screenshot from a simple order-confirmation screen. In the attached screenshot, a green check sits above "ORDER CONFIRMED"; central detail is the large text "REFERENCE PLK-2084"; smaller detail says "Pickup Friday at 3 PM". Keep the attached image dominant in conversation. Cobalt selection surrounds ONLY "REFERENCE PLK-2084" INSIDE the screenshot, not Alex's ordinary copyable message. The result snippet says exactly "REFERENCE PLK-2084". Need visibly nested screenshot attachment inside Slack. No real private messages or contact info, no claim of official Slack integration or endorsement.

Example 3: text rendered inside a canvas in a browser-based app, so dragging normally moves the canvas rather than selects text.
Exact headline: "When dragging won't copy."
Exact supporting line: "Select the screen. Get the text."
Source is a large realistic desktop browser window, address "canvasboard.example/view", showing a fictional web design-review app called "Canvasboard". Modest dark toolbar with tool icons, a narrow left sidebar "Layers" and a central soft gray zoomable canvas with a designed report card, all obviously software on a computer. The report card includes a small blue chart and the large exact field "ACCOUNT ID" above "AC-74029". The card is a graphical canvas object, not an input field. Small bottom canvas zoom indicator "100%". Blue selection surrounds only "AC-74029" within the graphic. Result snippet contains exactly "AC-74029". No disabled text message, no padlocks or security bypass imagery, no claim of hacking. The usefulness is extracting on-screen pixels from a canvas-rendered label.

Example 4: scanned PDF viewed inside a browser.
Exact headline: "Scanned PDF. Copyable text."
Exact supporting line: "Grab the detail you need."
Source is a large credible browser PDF viewer with tab "Invoice.pdf", address "files.example/Invoice.pdf", PDF toolbar "1 / 1" and "100%", a narrow page-thumbnail rail and gray viewer background. The scanned page is front-facing in the viewer and clearly an image scan: subtle paper grain, faint scanner shadow around page edges, tiny printed invoice table and a small rubber-stamp impression. No photographed tabletop, physical props, fingers or perspective tilt. Fictional invoice header "NORTHSTAR STUDIO", prominent field "INVOICE INV-1048", simple rows e.g. "Design services" and "$480.00". The screen selection surrounds only "INVOICE INV-1048". Result snippet contains exactly "INVOICE INV-1048". The source document needs surrounding PDF/browser controls so this is unmistakably a computer workflow rather than photographing paper.
